title: The images of tensor powers form an internal direct sum
statement: theorem graded_image_internal (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : DirectSum.IsInternal (fun n : ℕ => ((TensorAlgebra.ι R : M →ₗ[R] TensorAlgebra R M).range ^ n).map (algHom R M).toLinearMap)

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra, line 2165): T(M) is the direct sum of the T^n(M) with T^n * T^m in T^{n+m}; Sym(M) is the quotient of T(M) by the two-sided ideal generated by the degree-2 elements x (x) y - y (x) x, and Sym^n(M) is the image of T^n(M) (the text writes 'the image of a pure tensor x_1 (x) ... (x) x_n in Sym^n(M)'); the grading of the quotient by an ideal generated by homogeneous elements is used there without statement

proof.text: Identify each image with `(ι R M).range ^ n`. Construct a graded direct-sum algebra map by lifting the degree-one inclusion and prove by `Submodule.pow_induction_on_left'` that each power maps to its corresponding direct-sum component; `DirectSum.Decomposition.isInternal` then gives internality.
